Find ${lim}_{x\to 1}\frac{-2f(x)}{3{x}^{2}}$ for the function $f(x)$ plotted above.
question.worked_solution:
Using the quotient rule, we have

$$
{lim}_{x\to 1}\frac{-2f(x)}{3{x}^{2}}=\frac{{lim}_{x\to 1}(-2f(x))}{{lim}_{x\to 1}3{x}^{2}}.
$$

We find from the graph that ${lim}_{x\to 1}f(x)=6.$ Calculating the limits of the numerator and denominator separately, we have

$$
{lim}_{x\to 1}(-2f(x))=-2(6)=-12
$$

and

$$
{lim}_{x\to 1}3{x}^{2}=3(1)^{2}=3.
$$

Taking the quotient of these limits, we have
 

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to 1}\frac{-2f(x)}{3{x}^{2}} & =\frac{{lim}_{x\to 1}(-2f(x))}{{lim}_{x\to 1}3{x}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{-12}{3} \\  & =-4\,.\end{aligned}
$$
